title: RTM verification verdict
description: Contract for .arbiter/evidence/rtm/<REQ-NNN>.json — the evidence a FEATURE_MATRIX row must carry before it may claim `Verified`. Enforced by scripts/check-feature-matrix.mjs (INV-112, #2480). `Verified` was previously a word someone typed; this makes it a claim with a transcript behind it, the same fail-closed posture INV-146 applies to milestone `done`.

feature_id.description: Must equal the row this envelope stands under. A mismatch means the evidence was copied from another requirement, which is how a green row ends up proving something else.

verdict.description: The vocabulary forma's traceability lens already renders. Only PROVEN admits a `Verified` row; the other four are recordable states, not failures to hide — a requirement known to be FAILING is better governance than one silently left at Partial.

justification.description: Why the cited evidence establishes the claim. A verdict with no argument is an opinion with a schema around it, so the length floor is deliberate: it is not satisfied by 'works'.

command.description: The command actually executed to produce the transcript. PROVEN means something was RUN, not that someone read the code and was satisfied.

transcript_digest.description: sha256 of the executed command's output. The digest is not re-verifiable offline by design — its job is to make the claim falsifiable and attributable, not to re-run CI inside a lint gate.

citations.description: Where the proof lives, in axis 1's pinned-span grammar (`path#Lx-Ly@<12 hex>`) so a citation that drifts is reported OUTDATED by the same mechanism rather than a second one.

recorded_at.description: When the verdict was taken. A verdict has an age, and an old PROVEN over code that has since moved is what the citation pins exist to expose.
